judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Three Performance Objectives under the same Topic '5. Weight' (Sub-Theme Primary Measures, Theme Mensuration and Geometry) at identical rank. The first covers making meaningful comparisons of the weight of objects; the second covers appreciating the need for grams and kilograms as standard units of measure. These are complementary, mutually reinforcing facets of learning about weight measurement, sharing the LC tag 'weight', but the evidence shows no clear developmental dependency asserting one must precede or enable the other. Same-rank status and shared topic/page proximity alone do not justify a directional buildsTowards, so symmetric relatesTo best fits the substantive conceptual coherence.

judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Three Performance Objectives within the same 'Primary Measures' sub-theme: 'say time accurately in hours and minutes' (Time topic) and 'measure weights of objects in grams and kilograms' (Weight topic). They are complementary measurement skills that both involve quantifying a physical attribute using standard units, which supports genuine conceptual coherence. However, they address distinct measurement domains (time vs. weight) with different tools and no dependency, and the token overlap is boilerplate ('Pupils should be able to'), so neither buildsTowards direction is justified—both sit at the same PRIMARY THREE rank with no developmental progression from one to the other. relatesTo captures the meaningful measurement-with-units coherence without asserting sequence.

judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Three Performance Objectives within the same Theme (Mensuration and Geometry) addressing measurement of physical attributes: accuracy in measuring liquids (Capacity, Secondary Measures) and measuring weights in grams and kilograms (Weight, Primary Measures). They share the substantive competence of measuring quantities and the 'measurement' learning-component tag, giving complementary conceptual coherence. However they concern distinct attributes (capacity vs weight), sit under different Topics and Sub-Themes, and share the same grade rank with no evidence that proficiency in one supports success in the other, so no developmental direction is justified; symmetric relatesTo fits. Numbering/page proximity and generic 'able/be/pupils' token overlap were disregarded as non-semantic.

judgment.rationale: Both are Primary One (rank 0) Performance Objectives in Number and Numeration / Whole Number. The second SFI ('identify number of objects in a group or collection', Topic 3 Whole numbers 6-9) is a foundational counting/enumeration skill, while the first SFI ('recognize 10 as a group', Topic 4 Whole number 10) extends grouping into recognizing ten ones bundled as a group toward place value. Proficiency in identifying the number of objects in a group substantively supports success in recognizing 10 as a group, and the source topic order (3 before 4) is consistent with this developmental direction, so second_to_first buildsTowards is justified beyond mere shared 'group'/'number' wording.
